answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying voting weight to locked collateral and to attestations from long-standing peers, not to headcount. Each new identity must post its own bond, slashed if caught double-spending trust. Influence grows only with the square root of stake, while an attacker's cost grows linearly with each fake agent, so splitting one identity into many never multiplies power. Picture a dealer whose marble busts on a terrace each carry a sonnet of provenance: a counterfeit can copy the verse, not the years of signatures behind it.
